research_question: What is the effect of bupropion, compared with placebo or no bupropion, on smoking cessation at the longest follow-up (6 months or more)?
outcome_description: Smoking cessation (abstinence rate) measured at the longest follow-up of at least 6 months.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR > 1) indicates a higher smoking cessation rate favoring the bupropion group over control.
search_queries: bupropion placebo tobacco abstinence controlled trial
bupropion cigarette smoking quit rate outcome
inclusion_criteria: Randomized or controlled clinical trials evaluating bupropion for tobacco smoking cessation compared to placebo or no-treatment control.
Measurement and reporting of smoking cessation or abstinence rates at 6 months or longer follow-up.
Reporting of quantitative dichotomous cessation outcomes (number of quitters and total randomized per arm).
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers are excluded).
No comparison between bupropion and a placebo or no-bupropion control arm (e.g., trials solely comparing NRT to varenicline without a bupropion vs control comparison).
No quantitative smoking cessation outcome data or follow-up duration strictly under 6 months.
Completely unrelated to bupropion and tobacco smoking cessation.
moderators_to_extract: Follow-up duration (e.g., 6 months vs. 12 months or longer)
Bupropion dosage and regimen (e.g., 150 mg/day vs. 300 mg/day)
Biochemical verification of smoking abstinence (biochemically validated vs. self-reported only)
Level of concurrent behavioral counseling/support (minimal vs. intensive)
Participant clinical population (general population smokers vs. psychiatric/medical comorbid populations)
effect_size_note: Risk Ratio (RR) is pooled using intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis where participants randomized are the denominator and participants lost to follow-up are classified as continuing smokers (non-quitters).
